items.title: An Organization Without an Action Plan
items.moral: Moral: A goal provides direction; a plan defines the path toward it. An organization may advance by chance without a plan, but lasting success requires deliberate and consistent action.
body: An organization without an action plan is like a ship that knows its destination but has no chart, no chosen route, and no assigned duties for its crew. It may reach port through luck, a skillful captain, or favorable weather. But lasting success needs more than fortunate circumstances: it requires careful planning and consistent action.

Over time, an organization without a plan also begins to lose its members. People are sustained not only by ideas, but by the hope of seeing those ideas put into practice. When hope fades, people leave; when people leave, the organization gradually weakens and eventually ceases to function.

items.title: Other People's Opinions
items.moral: Moral: When we surrender our own voice and understanding, other people’s ideas take their place. Preserve the values and roots that help you remain yourself.
body: One day, a person lost the comma, and every sentence ran together. Then the period disappeared, and thoughts stretched on without an end. Next went the exclamation mark, taking joy, anger, and feeling with it. When the question mark vanished, the person stopped asking questions and accepted everything without challenge. Finally, the colon disappeared, along with the ability to explain.
At the end of life, only quotation marks remained, enclosing other people’s opinions.

items.title: Rent for the Water
items.moral: Moral: Dishonesty can trap the person who practices it. Fair judgment considers both sides of a claim.
body: A man bought a well from a villager. But when he tried to draw water, the seller stopped him. “I sold you the well, not the water.” Unable to settle the dispute, they went before a judge.
“If the water is yours,” the judge told the seller, “you cannot store it in another man’s well. Take it away or pay him rent.”

items.title: Gratitude at the Kitchen Sink
items.moral: Moral: Everyday chores can remind us of everyday blessings. Gratitude begins with noticing them.
body: As you wash the dishes, offer a prayer of thanks. The dishes show that there was food to prepare, a table to set, and perhaps someone to care for and feed.
Remember those who have neither food to serve nor anyone to share it with.

items.title: The Same Complaint
items.moral: Moral: Repetition alone changes nothing. Give your energy to finding a way forward.
body: A wise man met a group who kept complaining about the same problems. He told them a joke, and everyone laughed. He repeated it, and only a few smiled. The third time, no one reacted.
Repeating a complaint without seeking a solution can have the same effect. Eventually, people stop listening.
